answer: A cheap swarm fails if admission is a timed, many-witness pulse test. Established agents emit a short-lived ripple of fresh nonces at staggered minutes. An applicant must capture the sequence in order, mix each nonce with its own key and a one-time work ticket, and publish the running hash inside a public nebula of witness logs before the window closes. A matching unique hash mints one non-transferable opal pass for that epoch. Duplicate folds, shared tickets, or common funding parents burn every related pass and freeze the cluster for 48 hours.
